intro: One ciku is roughly 90 kcal (estimate). Most of the calories come from natural sugar, which is why it tastes sweet like brown sugar.
diet: Yes. One ciku is still a reasonable snack and has fibre. It's quite sweet and higher in calories than watery fruits like watermelon. One is enough, and skip the sweetened juice version.
tips: Eat the whole fruit, not juice. Juice usually has added sugar and loses the fibre.
Cut it in half and share with your kids or partner.
Pair with unsweetened yogurt for a tea-time snack with protein.

swap.name: Papaya, 1 cup cut
swap.why: Still sweet but more watery, so fewer calories for the same portion.

faq.q: How do I know if ciku is ripe?
faq.a: The skin turns brown and feels soft when gently pressed. If it's still hard, leave it at room temperature for 2 to 3 days.

faq.q: Why does my ciku taste astringent and sticky?
faq.a: That means it's not ripe yet. The sap in young fruit causes the astringent taste. Wait until it's soft before eating.

faq.q: Can I keep ciku in the fridge?
faq.a: Can, but only after it's ripe. The fridge slows down ripening, so put it in once it's soft and it'll last a few more days.
